normal_speed_reason: No actual normal-speed playback viewing surface was available in this review. Images were inspected; neither sampled frames nor decoding would establish normal-speed viewing.
one_gap_that_matters_most: The five leg strokes form long, nearly parallel poles in every key. They do not carry the source’s changing front-leg reach and bent/receding leg poses, especially during the turn toward camera. This is the main break in pose correspondence.
smallest_repair: Keep exactly five sparse leg strokes and the present body/head treatment. Change only the leg attachment positions, lengths, angles, and occasional bends across the six keys so the front group follows the visible reaching/bending front legs and the rear pair recedes as in the corresponding source poses. Retain the original doodle’s uneven dangling-stroke character instead of making an evenly spaced parallel bundle.
strengths_not_to_lose: The pig remains clearly recognizable as the supplied doodle: angular double-peak ears, nested square spiral snout, sparse black outline, and five leg strokes.
The left-facing profile develops toward a three-quarter frontal view, with the snout moving through approximately the right areas of the source frame.
The large right-side body crop and simple fence/ground context preserve the broad source composition.
scope_limit: Static composition, sampled pose correspondence, and drawing identity only; no timing, interpolation, or motion approval.
